title: Level 1 project: a game inventory
lesson:
A real piece of a game: the **inventory**, written as a plain C# class you could drop into a Unity project as-is.

Make `public class Inventory` with:
1. A constructor `Inventory(int maxSlots)`: how many different items fit.
2. `bool Add(string item, int count)`: adds `count` of an item (names are case-insensitive: "Arrow" and "arrow" are the same, stored lowercase). Adding a NEW item when all slots are used fails and returns false; adding more of an item you already have always works. Count must be at least 1 (else `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`).
3. `int Take(string item, int count)`: removes up to `count`, frees the slot at 0, returns how many were taken.
4. `int CountOf(string item)` and the property `int SlotsUsed`.
5. `override string ToString()`: items alphabetically as `arrow x15, potion x2`, or `(empty)`.

Plan the field first (a `Dictionary<string, int>` works), then each method, checking as you go.

Next: **Level 2** (interfaces, inheritance, events, generics, unit testing) — and if you want, a Unity track where these classes become MonoBehaviours.

exercises.title: The inventory
exercises.prompt: Build Inventory as described in the lesson. All the tests must pass.

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var i = new Inventory(3); i.Add("Arrow", 10); i.Add("arrow", 5); i.Add("Potion", 2); return i.ToString() + " | " + i.SlotsUsed; }))()
tests.name: add and print

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var i = new Inventory(1); bool a = i.Add("sword", 1); bool b = i.Add("shield", 1); bool c = i.Add("Sword", 1); return a + " " + b + " " + c + " " + i.CountOf("SWORD"); }))()
tests.name: slots are limited

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var i = new Inventory(2); i.Add("potion", 2); int t = i.Take("potion", 5); return t + " " + i.SlotsUsed + " " + i; }))()
tests.name: take frees the slot

hints: Fields: private readonly Dictionary<string, int> items = new(); private readonly int maxSlots;
Add: key = item.ToLowerInvariant(); if (!items.ContainsKey(key) && items.Count >= maxSlots) return false;
ToString: items.Count == 0 ? "(empty)" : string.Join(", ", items.OrderBy(kv => kv.Key).Select(kv => $"{kv.Key} x{kv.Value}"))

choices: So 'Arrow' and 'arrow' are the same item
